subsections.tex: \subsection{Formal structure of the article}\label{subsec:formal} We prove three main theorems, stated and labeled as \ref{them:a}, \ref{them:b}, and \ref{them:c} in this introduction and proved in the order~\ref{them:c},~\ref{them:a},~\ref{them:b} in the paper; see also their interdependence in Figure \ref{fig:un}, where appears also the Main Theorem of a companion paper \cite{BouJui2}. Theorem \ref{them:a} answers the Main Problem p.\,\pageref{problem} below, and is a general theoretical result in Probability Theory; it builds a certain stochastic process with given marginals: the \emph{Markov-quantile} process. Theorem \ref{them:b} gives a convergence result to it. Theorems \ref{them:c} presents an application of the Markov-quantile process to another context (Martingales and a theorem of Kellerer \cite{Ke72,Ke73}), giving by the way the Main Problem additional motivations, see Section~\ref{subsec:intro_kellerer} and Figure \ref{fig:un}. We also prove Theorem \ref{them:sous_n}, linked with Theorem \ref{them:c}. Being a bit more technical, it is not stated in this introduction. Another application (to Optimal Transport and the Continuity Equation) in presented in \cite{BouJui2}.
